blocks.text: Continuity Worlds are reflected by strata, fossils, tree rings, glaciers, cairns, archives, ancestral roads, and places whose meaning depends on what remains through change.
Wild Worlds are reflected by reefs, wetlands, migrating islands, fire ecologies, forests, grasslands, predator-prey systems, succession, and landscapes that cannot be reduced to a finished design.
Crafted Worlds are reflected by terraces, gardens, resonant canyons, stepwells, engineered weather, civic water systems, responsive architecture, and physical law used as collaborative art.
Pilgrim Worlds are reflected by passes, roads, islands, waystations, body-change environments, underways, and distances that transform the traveler rather than merely transport them.
Quiet Worlds are reflected by fog forests, caves, slow archives, restricted observation, deep ice, sheltered ecologies, and places that resist constant access.
Open Worlds are reflected by ports, markets, shared cities, crossroads, translation halls, civic reservoirs, and places maintained through exchange among unlike inhabitants.
These are traditions rather than exclusive nations. A place can belong to several at once, change its emphasis across eras, or preserve only a fragment of an older tradition.
